brief: Ukraine's open-banking and state-rail landscape is unusually regulator-anchored: the NBU publishes the regime (Regulation on Open Banking, Board Resolution No. 80 of 25.07.2025, in force 01.08.2025 with an ASPSP compliance deadline of 01.01.2026), the Payment Infrastructure Register lists authorised TPPs and technology operators, and the SEP pages date the instant-payment rollout from SEP-4.1 (01.12.2024) — together giving a dated spine against which vendor activity can be timed. Vendor identity, however, is published almost entirely by suppliers rather than buyers: Open API Hub (EMA + GD Next) and UPC (with Tietoevry, Berlin Group NextGenPSD2) name their bank partners on their own sites, Salt Edge courts the market through co-hosted webinars, and every ASPSP's own Open API page discloses its standard and go-live. The state-digital leg is well documented and quantified through integration.diia.gov.ua and Mintsifra, which publish bank integration counts and, since 2025, a paid tariff for bank document-sharing. The main structural weaknesses are the absence of any public pilot-participant list (the authorisation register is the real artefact), no disclosed supplier for the NBU's own SEP core, and the fact that most Ukrainian banks are private and so leave no Prozorro trace — pushing vendor attribution toward conference recaps, job ads and vendor self-reporting.
